parts:
Hello all,
I am trying to conduct multiple mean and covariance structure analysis with lavaan for my bifactor model (see below) and I have some troubles with it. I have 4-point ordinal data, so I am using DWLS estimator with WLSMV correction. 

1) I have the bifactor model with phantom variables. The model specification: 8 specific latent variables (AVM, AXM, AVF, AXF, AVP, AXP, AVBF, AXBF) and 2 global factors (gv, gx), I specified a phantom variable for every latent variable (AVMph, AXMph...). The configural and weak invariance are estimating without any problem. In the next steps 2 problems are occuring:

a) When I am trying to fix thresholds -  intercepts are estimated for both original latent variable (AVM) and phantom variable (AVMph), which they shouldn´t, right? Then I have 10 more free parameters in model with phantom variables in comparison to the same model but without phantom variables.

b) When I am trying to fix residuals -   fit indexes and degrees of freedom are the same as in the previous step, nothing is changing and residuals are freely estimated in both groups.

messages.author: ad188126f9138663
messages.subject: Re: Measurement invariance - phantom variables and residuals fixing
parts:
Aneta,
  If I follow your question correctly, you are using the theta parameterization for ordinal variables and want to compare a model with loadings and thresholds constrained to equality across groups to a second model which further constrains the residuals to be equal.  My understanding is that this refers to the residuals on the latent continuous variables that underly the ordered observed variables.  Further, the distinguishing feature of the theta parameterization is that it fixes these residual variances to unity.  As a result, constraining them to equality will add no further constraints to the model.  That is why your degrees of freedom do not change.

  I am not sure what you mean by fixing thresholds.  The group.equal parameter imposes equality constraints across groups but does not fix the parameters.  These are free parameters in both the theta and delta parameterizaitons.

  If that does not answer your questions, then my suggestion would be to work out a minimally sufficient example to illustrate the problem that you are trying to solve.  Also, questions about measurement invariance with ordered variables are quite frequent in this forum.  So, you can find discussion of best practices with references by searching related threads.

Keith
